blocks.text: El Panecillo hill and its statue overlooking the colourful houses of Quito, Ecuador
Quito: a green hill and monument overlooking historic façades

After breakfast, set out on a sightseeing tour of Quito that includes a visit to the equator.

Quito sits at an elevation of approximately 2,800 m.

The historic centre retains its colonial-era churches, domes, squares and buildings.

Your guide will tell you about the city’s architecture, art, culture, legends and traditions.

The Quito School of art brought together Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and local traditions.

The walk through the Old Town takes about an hour and a half.

Plaza Grande is home to the cathedral, the Presidential Palace, the Archbishop’s Palace and City Hall.

You’ll visit the Jesuit church, one of the city’s finest examples of colonial art.

Another major stop is the Basílica del Voto Nacional.

The basilica is considered one of Ecuador’s most prominent examples of Gothic Revival architecture. Its design is associated with the influence of European Gothic architecture.

Instead of traditional gargoyles, the façades feature animals found in Ecuador, including caimans, turtles, boobies and monkeys.

The church is 140 m long and 35 m wide, and its central nave is about 30 m high.

Another viewpoint is El Panecillo hill, topped by a statue of the winged Virgin Mary.

After the city tour, continue to the Middle of the World.

The itinerary includes two separate sites.

The visitor complex is associated with the geodetic expedition of 1736.

The current monument, about 30 m high, was erected between 1979 and 1982.

Later GPS measurements placed the actual equator about 240 m north of the monument.
